regime_context: The detector shows a clear precious-metals leadership cluster (Gold Miners rank 1, score 2.143, durability 0.82 hurst 'trend'; Silver & Royalties rank 2, score 1.772) with broad eligibility (11/16 themes eligible) but no single narrative dominance and modest absorption (0.31). Given track_record dir_accuracy is only 0.278 (worse than coin-flip) and the validated edge is only drawdown control, I am keeping conviction low and leaning only on the strongest, gate-confirmed trend leg.
emerging_watch: Watching whether the metals leadership broadens from Gold/Silver into Base Metals & Copper: if XBM.TO (Base Metals) begins closing the score gap on XGD.TO while its crowding flag clears, the clean two-theme precious-metals cluster becomes a broader materials complex — but I will only treat this as a confirmed handoff, not predict it.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners is the ranking leader with the strongest trend-health profile in the whole table: durability_bar 0.82, hurst_tag 'trend', breadth 1.0, and it is eligible under the absolute-trend gate (the one validated leg). This is not a return forecast but a staying-power read — the only theme combining top rank with clean trend classification.
evidence: eligible true under absolute-trend gate (the validated risk-control leg)
breadth 1.0, crowded false — full participation without crowding flag
theses.dissent: The cross-sectional rank has no forward return edge (~rank-IC 0), and precious metals can gap violently on macro surprise; past high-conviction calls from this desk have hit at only a 55.6% rate with 27.8% directional accuracy, so leadership persistence may not translate into further relative gains over 20 days.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO lags the S&P/TSX by 5% before the check-by date

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties
theses.thesis: Silver & Royalties is the rotation challenger (rank 2, score 1.772) and shares the precious-metals leadership cluster with Gold Miners. Its durability_bar 0.76 and full breadth suggest the metals leadership is cohesive rather than a single-name spike, but hurst_tag 'mixed' means the trend is less clean than Gold Miners, capping conviction.
evidence: rank 2, score 1.772, rotation challenger to Gold Miners
same category as leader (Precious Metals) — cohesive cluster, not isolated
theses.dissent: Silver is far more industrial/cyclical than gold and can decouple from the gold bid; the theme's hurst_tag 'mixed' suggests weaker trend persistence than the leader, and the rotation margin (0.371) alone has no validated forward edge.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO (shared proxy) lags the S&P/TSX by 5% before the check-by date

theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: Base Metals & Copper ranks 3 and is eligible, but it is the only top-5 theme flagged crowded (crowding_z 1.11, crowded true) and its hurst_tag is 'mixed'. Crowding is a size-down caution only, never a fade — but given the desk's poor directional record, the cleanest expression of that caution is to avoid adding here, not to underweight the dominant metals complex.
evidence: rank 3, score 1.18, eligible true — relative strength present
crowding_z 1.11, crowded true — the only top-5 crowded flag
hurst_tag 'mixed' — weaker trend-health than Gold Miners
theses.dissent: Copper's fundamental supply story (electrification, grid build-out) is durable and independent of the precious-metals bid; the crowding flag has no basket-level forward edge and only down-sizes, so avoiding entirely could forgo legitimate trend participation in a broad metals complex.

falsifier.text: XBM.TO outperforms XGD.TO by 5% before the check-by date
